Architecture conditions behind the isolated MSI hook and when it reports true.
Virtual interrupt lifetime and lookup behavior behind the default domain query.
Enabled lockup and hardlockup and hung task detector behavior, perf event setup, and buddy check semantics.
Backtrace emission mechanics, CPU mask handling, exclusion rules, and stall detection thresholds.
POSIX clock driver callback contracts, error codes, poll and control semantics, and zombie transition plus semaphore ordering.

findings.text: MSI domain behavior uses single bit selectors. Generic selectors occupy the low half from bit zero through bit ten and cover default operation installation, activation timing, reactivation, sysfs handling, descriptor allocation policy, firmware node use, power device propagation and parent mask and startup interaction. Domain selectors occupy bits sixteen through twenty two and cover multi message, extended message, level capability, contiguity, dynamic allocation, missing affinity and mask inhibition. The generic mask covers the low sixteen bits and the domain mask covers the high sixteen bits.
MSI chip behavior uses two single bit selectors starting at bit zero, one governing end of interrupt handling and one governing acknowledge handling.

Parent MSI description carries a supported flag word plus a required flag word plus a chip flag word plus bus selection token and mask plus a prefix string plus a boolean init callback. The callback receives a device pointer and two domain pointers and a child info pointer.
Count based MSI allocation is a convenience that requests a zero based contiguous interval ending one less than the requested count.

Isolated MSI query delegates to an architecture hook and returns its boolean result. Commentary treats lack of platform MSI reception as isolated by definition while noting the default hook stays conservative.
In this configuration PCI MSI device domain lookup yields null and MSI message write performs no action.
MSI domain identifiers provide a default domain first and a count sentinel second, implying one device domain in this view.
MSI instance cookie is a union that can hold either a sixty four bit integer value or an untyped pointer, allowing one cookie to carry either form.
MSI map is a small record pairing an allocation index with a virtual interrupt number, both held as signed integers.
Wildcard MSI index equals the maximum unsigned integer value and signals that any index is acceptable.
Device virtual interrupt lookup resolves the given index through the default domain.

POSIX clock operations hold an owner module pointer plus time adjust and time read and resolution read and time set hooks, plus optional file style hooks for control and open and poll and release and read that operate on a clock context.
POSIX clock embeds its operation table and character device node, points at a device object, and includes a read write semaphore plus a boolean zombie marker.
POSIX clock context links back to its parent clock and to the open file and to private driver data.
POSIX clock provides a read write semaphore for mutual exclusion and a zombie flag for end of life marking. Exact acquisition order and transition protocol are not shown.

CPU clock encoding uses thread marker four and selector mask three, with profile zero and virtual one and schedule two and maximum three. File descriptor clocks equal the maximum value and the combined mask merges thread and selector bits. Process identity is recovered by complementing the shifted value, thread mode is detected from the marker bit, and selector is obtained by masking low bits.

Clock identifier helpers encode a complemented process number shifted by three combined with a clock selector. The thread form adds the thread marker, the descriptor form uses the descriptor number with the file clock selector, the reverse helper inverts shift and complement to recover the descriptor, and the auxiliary test requires build configuration enable plus range membership.

CPU timer holds a queue node plus a pointer to its queue head plus a process identifier reference plus a list element plus a firing flag plus a nanosleep flag plus a task pointer for the current handler.

CPU timer queue state is idle when the stored head is null. Enqueue records the head and inserts the node, queued test reflects head presence, dequeue removes and clears and reports whether removal happened, and expiry lives in the node with dedicated read and write access.

CPU timers initialization clears the container then arms all three bases to the maximum unsigned value meaning no event. The scheduler watchdog updates only the schedule base to supplied runtime. Static initializers provide the same maximum for each base.

Alternate disabled configuration provides an empty timer type and empty timers type and empty static init. Group init and rearm and free and work init and work clear do nothing, signal delivery reports false, and privileged creation reports invalid argument.

Kernel interval timer splits into a read mostly head with hash and list nodes plus identifier plus clock selector plus notification mode plus pid type plus signal pointer plus clock operations pointer, and a mutable tail with spin lock plus status plus periodic flag plus overrun counters plus sequence counters plus interval plus ignored list plus pid or process union plus signal queue plus reference count plus a timer union for real high resolution or CPU or alarm variants plus an RCU head. The whole object is cache line aligned for multiprocessing.
Interval timer spin lock guards the mutable tail while the head stays mostly read only. A reference count governs lifetime with free on last drop and an RCU head permits deferred reclamation.

Timer validity is encoded in the least significant bit of the stored signal pointer, where a set bit means invalid, so the pointer must never be dereferenced without masking. Queue reference helpers derive the enclosing timer from its embedded queue and adjust the reference count, warning once if acquisition fails.
Disabled signal queue reference acquisition and release do nothing in the alternate configuration.

CPU timer base pairs a next event timestamp with a queue head. The timers container holds three such bases plus active and expiry counters. The work container holds a callback head plus a mutex plus a scheduled flag. An alternate configuration provides an empty timers type.
CPU timers work mutex serializes work handling while the scheduled flag tracks pending execution and the callback head links deferred work.
Scheduler clock read data holds epoch in nanoseconds and cycles plus a cycle mask plus a function returning the current cycle counter plus multiplier and shift for conversion.
Generic scheduler clock initialization performs no action in this configuration.

Tick broadcast modes are off then on then force, and broadcast states are exit then enter. Tick dependency bits run zero through five for POSIX timer and performance events and scheduler and unstable clock and RCU and expedited RCU. Maximum equals the last bit, none mask is zero, and each named mask is the single bit at its position.

Broadcast convenience wrappers map enable to on and disable to off and force to force through a common control, while enter and exit delegate to oneshot control with matching state and propagate the integer result where present.

Disabled tickless behavior reports enabled as zero and active as false and stopped as zero locally and per CPU. Idle stop and retain and restart and enter and exit do nothing and got tick reports false. Next timer is computed as now plus tick period and sleep length reports the tick period while storing it through the output parameter.

Full tickless enable either requires tracking plus a running flag or is constant false by configuration. Global set and clear act only when full is enabled, per CPU variants act only when the target CPU is full, task init clears the task mask, and task and signal set and clear follow the same gating. Per CPU nohz helpers do nothing in this view.

Watchdog and lockup lifecycle entries do nothing in this configuration, covering detector init and retry and soft poweroff, scheduler and direct and sync and global touches, hung task reset, hardlockup disable, architecture touch, performance stop and restart and configuration and period adjust, buddy check, timer threshold update, and stall snapshot and check. Backtrace sysctl controls read as zero and online and offline CPU hooks are null.
NMI watchdog touch fans out first to the architecture specific touch and then to the softlockup touch.

Backtrace triggers have an enabled form that emits through a mask helper for all CPUs or all but one or an explicit mask or a single CPU and reports success, and a disabled form that performs no action and reports failure.
Watchdog enable bits place hard detection at zero and soft detection at one, with each enable mask being the single bit at its position.

Tick lifecycle entries do nothing here, covering init and local suspend and resume and freeze and unfreeze and interrupt entry and broadcast pull on CPU removal plus a handover assertion. The dying CPU hook is null.

Many helpers succeed silently while disabled, including null domain lookup, zero tickless constants, empty detector and clock init, and empty queue reference handling, so callers must not assume hardware action occurred.
Each listed header defines a unique inclusion guard macro that prevents double inclusion.
